um_intro: Hleðsluverð compares the price of EV charging in Iceland: what a kilowatt-hour costs with each operator and at each station, which chargers are free, and how prices have changed.
um_independent: Hleðsluverð is independent and not affiliated with any of the charging operators it compares. We do our best to keep prices right, but the price that applies is always the one the operator states in its app or at the charger.
um_prices_title: Where do the prices come from?
um_prices_intro: Prices are fetched automatically every hour from the operator's own website or platform. Where that isn't possible, they are entered by hand.
um_fail_loud: If a price can't be read with confidence, for example after an operator redesigns its site, we don't guess. The last confirmed price stays in place until we fix the collection.
um_host_priced: At some stations, such as at hotels and shops, the site owner sets the price rather than the operator. That price shows on the station itself but is left out of the operator’s rate card and price trend.
um_verified: The "verified" date says when we last saw the price with the operator: the last time automatic collection read the same price, or when it was checked by hand. When a price changes we record the new one and keep the old one in the price history.
um_stale: hasn't been verified for more than 30 days. It may still be right, but we can't vouch for it.
um_estimate: When you choose a car on the front page, we fold per-minute fees into the kWh price and estimate the cost of charging from 10 % to 80 %. Car data (peak power and usable battery size) comes from our own list, compiled by hand from manufacturer spec sheets and other sources. It has no charging curves, so on DC the average power is assumed to be about 60 % of the car's peak, or 90 % of the charger's rating if it is slower. These figures are therefore marked ≈ and are estimates, not exact prices. Where data is missing we show nothing rather than guess.
um_avail: Charger availability comes from TomTom. It is cached for 5 minutes and always shown with its age, e.g. "2 min ago". "—" means the status is unknown, not that nothing is free; 0 means every charger is busy. Not every station has availability data from TomTom.
um_stations_intro: Station locations, connectors and power come from the following sources, which we gratefully credit:
um_src_ocm: the base of the station list. The data is contributed by Open Charge Map users and published under
um_src_virta: stations on the Ísorka charging network. Every site is reviewed by hand before it appears.
um_src_e1: stations and connectors from e1's public map, for operators that use e1's platform, such as Orkan.
um_src_supercharge: Tesla Superchargers missing from Open Charge Map, and their stall counts. Information there is neither provided nor validated by Tesla.
um_src_streetview: street-level photos of the stations on the "Near me" cards.
um_src_places: photos of the stations on the map (Places UI Kit).
um_src_cars: Cars: connectors, peak power and battery size come from our own list, compiled by hand from manufacturer spec sheets, Wikipedia, Fastned, ev-database.org and the EV press. Every car lists the sources it was checked against.
um_src_map: base map, built on OpenStreetMap data:
um_stations_sync: The station list is refreshed from these sources once a day.
um_contact_report: Seen a wrong price, a closed station or wrong availability? The quickest way is "Report a wrong price" at the bottom of that station's page.

um_nearby: "Near me" shows the 20 nearest stations with their price per kWh. The order weighs distance and price per kWh, with distance counting for more. A per-minute fee charged from the first minute counts towards the order; a fee that only starts after a set time, e.g. after 1 h, does not, and is shown on the station's card. Under "Full charge" on each card is the estimated cost and time of charging from 0 % to 100 %. The time uses one average power for the whole charge: on DC 80 % of the car's or the station's peak, but never more than about 1.1 kW per kWh of battery, because the last 20 % charges slowly. On AC it is the power of the car's on-board charger. Per-minute fees are worked out from that time, and charging losses are included: about 8 % on DC and 12 % on AC.
